title: Adaptive surge-resilient commit with operator checkpoints for Optimize suggestions
creator: Asha Verma
description:
Goal: implement a surge-resilient automated commit path for Optimize recommendations (batching and KV cache profiles) that prevents blast radius during sudden traffic changes, surfaces operator checkpoints, and enables fast, observable rollback when regressions are detected.

Scope:
- A telemetry-driven commit controller that senses request-throughput and latency spikes and pauses or throttles suggestion applies during surges.
- A lightweight micro-rollout (canary) mode that activates a new config on a controlled fraction of traffic with early-signal probing.
- Operator checkpoint hooks (email/console notifications + a manual latch) before progressing beyond 10%/50%/100% ramps.
- Safe rollback path with automated snapshot of prior config, immediate revert API, and postmortem hooks.

Non-goals:
- Building a full A/B testing experimentation framework (out of scope for this ticket).
- Long-term UI polish for the rollout editor (we'll ship a minimal console view this cycle).
acceptance_criteria: Controller halts or throttles suggestion commits when latency or error rate exceeds configured surge thresholds within 10 seconds of detection
Micro-rollout supports percent-based traffic splits: 1%, 10%, 50%, 100% and advances automatically only when health signals pass configured thresholds

Operator checkpoint notification appears in Console and sends an assertion email to on-call when moving from 10% -> 50% and 50% -> 100%, with the option to require manual approval (configurable per-customer)
Rollback API reverts to the previously active config within 15s and records a telemetry event for causal analysis
End-to-end integration tests validate surge protection by simulating a 3x traffic spike and asserting controller pauses auto-apply and triggers rollback path
notes:
Design choices and trade-offs: we prioritized a fast, observable safety net over full automation. Instead of hard auto-reverting on any anomaly, the controller will: (1) throttle the commit, (2) escalate to operator checkpoint if metrics don't recover, and (3) perform an automated revert only if critical SLOs are breached (configurable). This reduces noisy rollbacks for non-actionable transient spikes.

On telemetry: we'll reuse the existing per-route latency and error rate probes (trace-backed) but add a short-term aggregation window (10s) to detect surges. Chosen thresholds are conservative by default (latency 2x baseline or error rate +3pcts) and exposed to customer override.

Implementation plan: 
- Week A: controller core + surge detector + API to start/stop rollouts (Daniel)
- Week B: micro-rollout traffic splitter + checkpoint notifications (Asha)
- Week C: rollback API + integration tests + end-to-end smoke (team)

Open questions: 
- Should the controller pre-warm fallback model variants during a rollback path to reduce cold-start latency? (ops + infra input needed)
- Default threshold values: we will run a 1-week internal canary on staging to tune.

Decision log:
- Use percent-based micro-rollouts (vs. user-id hashing) to keep splits simple and compatible with existing routing.
- Operator checkpoints are enabled by default for enterprise tenants, optional for self-serve tenants.
